title: Concord mapper: OpenAI Chat->Redwood request/response shape translator
creator: Maya Johnson
description: Implement a reliability-preserving compatibility mapper that accepts OpenAI Chat Completions (both synchronous and streaming) and produces equivalent Redwood API request/response shapes. The mapper must handle tool/function calling semantics, structured JSON outputs, stop-sequences, delta/stream framing, and provenance metadata while preserving determinism for downstream telemetry and evals. This ticket covers design decisions, edge-case handling, integration tests, and a lightweight shim for the gateway to use in canary deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Translator accepts OpenAI-style request payloads (messages, temperature, top_p, max_tokens, functions) and maps to Redwood request fields without losing semantic information
Streaming path preserves token-level deltas and tool-invocation events: hedging events must be idempotent and include stable provenance ids
Function/tool call lifecycle works end-to-end: selection, arguments JSON, synthetic assistant messages, and client-visible finish_reason mapping
Structured output mode: canonicalize 'content' with JSON schema enforcement path for both assistant and tool responses and surface validation errors in telemetry
Backward-compatibility toggles: opt-in strict-mode (emulate legacy OA behavior) and best-effort mode (convert to Redwood canonical shapes) with config flags
Comprehensive test harness with 120+ fixtures covering streaming reassembly, truncated tool args, concurrent tool calls, and malformed user messages
Telemetry emits mapping decisions, dropped fields, transformation costs, and latency breakdowns for each request
Performance: median mapping overhead < 3ms p50 and < 10ms p95 under synthetic load; CPU and memory budget documented
Rollout plan and canary script available for Console to exercise real traffic and automatic fallback to native handling
